Maximum torque check: let R = r₂/s and Z = √(r₁²+(x₁+x₂)²). At R = Z the denominator is 2Z(Z+r₁), so T_max = (p/ω)·3V²/{2[r₁+Z]}. This does not contain r₂, which confirms the explanation.
Because torque is a function of r₂/s, multiplying r₂ by k produces the same torque at k times the slip. This is proportional shifting (比例推移), and it is consistent with blanks (ウ) 二次 and (エ) 比例推移.
